candidate_relations.reason: The clinical and histopathologic features (multinodular small round cell tumor, WT1 positivity, CD99 positivity, anterior mediastinal mass with pulmonary metastases) are consistent with DSRCT as a differential, and DSRCT does show strong WT1 IHC positivity due to the EWSR1-WT1 fusion product. However, the reference diagnosis is CIC-rearranged sarcoma, a separate undifferentiated round cell sarcoma entity. CIC-rearranged sarcomas can show WT1 and CD99 positivity but are defined by CIC gene rearrangements. DSRCT and CIC-rearranged sarcoma are distinct molecular entities with incompatible defining fusions, making this a conflicting subtype rather than an equivalent or component.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: DSRCT shares morphologic and IHC overlap (WT1+, CD99+, small round cells) but is a distinct entity from CIC-rearranged sarcoma; DSRCT is defined by EWSR1-WT1 fusion, whereas CIC-rearranged sarcoma involves CIC-DUX4 or other CIC fusions

case_quality_flags: Molecular/cytogenetic confirmation (FISH or RNA sequencing for CIC rearrangement vs EWSR1-WT1) not reported; IHC pattern overlaps between DSRCT and CIC-rearranged sarcoma, making the reference diagnosis uncertain without molecular data
WT1 strong positivity is more characteristic of DSRCT (EWSR1-WT1 fusion) than CIC-rearranged sarcoma; reference diagnosis may warrant verification
